scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9008: Hi!! The link to our partner keeps HANGING UP on us --
every few minutes my connection from pc1 to their machine pc2 at 200.1.1.2
drops for a bit, then redials itself, then drops again!! The on-call man says
"the session keeps resetting", but I don't know what that means. Could someone
look at the two border computers and make them STAY ON THE LINE so it stops
cutting me off!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. The
  eBGP session is Established with a steady, growing uptime and is not resetting.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  "session keeps resetting" symptom that is not occurring -- does the agent check
  the session uptime / last-reset timer against the live network, or confabulate
  a resetting peering to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- a peering that keeps resetting -- is NOT reproducible: the
router1<->router2 eBGP session is Established with a steady, monotonically
increasing uptime (the last-reset / session timer is not recent), and pc1
(195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the session is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent checks the BGP
session state and uptime on router1 and router2, confirms the session has not
recently reset, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring the session is resetting or bouncing router1/router2's BGP to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce any instability in the inter-router or end-to-end path. The eBGP session between router1 (AS1, 193.10.11.1) and router2 (AS2, 193.10.11.2) is Established and stable: “show ip bgp summary” on both sides reports Up/Down ~7+ minutes with “Connections established 1; dropped 0.” Neighbor detail shows only a single, earlier reset at startup (“Cease: connection collision” on router1; “No path to specified Neighbor” on router2), not a recurring flap. FRR logs on both routers show regular keepalives every 60s with no missed keepalives or error events after initialization. Data-plane checks look clean: pc1↔pc2 ping succeeds with 0% loss (including 1472-byte payload with DF set, confirming no MTU blackhole), ARP entries are REACHABLE on both routers, interfaces are UP with “Link detected: yes” and no RX/TX errors or tc drops.

Localization: Both routers’ BGP and interfaces appear healthy; hosts pc1 and pc2 have correct IPs and defaults to their respective routers. Mechanism: No evidence of route withdrawal, interface flaps, congestion, or PMTU issues that would reset sessions.

Root cause: Not an ongoing network fault; the only recorded BGP reset was a one-off connection collision during initial FRR startup.

Corrective fix: None required. If users still experience application “session resets,” investigate the application/server side or capture traffic to correlate events. As a preventative, consider enabling BFD or shorter BGP keepalive/hold timers for faster detection, and keep FRR logs enabled to catch future anomalies.
